**Runtime Detection**

`[Supported fact]` `PRAGMA module_list;` returns the list of virtual-table modules registered with the current database connection. FTS5 is an SQLite virtual-table module. (https://sqlite.org/pragma.html , https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Inference]` If `fts5` appears in `PRAGMA module_list`, FTS5 is available on that connection at that moment; this follows from “module_list returns registered virtual-table modules” plus “FTS5 is a virtual-table module.” (https://sqlite.org/pragma.html , https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Supported fact]` `PRAGMA compile_options;` returns the compile-time options used to build SQLite, one per row, and omits the `SQLITE_` prefix. (https://sqlite.org/pragma.html)

`[Supported fact]` `SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5` adds FTS5 to the build automatically when that option is defined for the amalgamation build. (https://sqlite.org/compile.html)

`[Inference]` So, in `PRAGMA compile_options`, the relevant marker for a built-in FTS5 build is `ENABLE_FTS5`. (https://sqlite.org/pragma.html , https://sqlite.org/compile.html)

`[Supported fact]` In C, `sqlite3_compileoption_used()` returns `0` or `1` depending on whether a named compile-time option was defined, and the `SQLITE_` prefix may be omitted when calling that C API. (https://sqlite.org/c3ref/compileoption_get.html)

`[Supported fact]` In SQL, `sqlite_compileoption_used()` is a wrapper around `sqlite3_compileoption_used()`. (https://sqlite.org/lang_corefunc.html)

`[Supported fact]` FTS5 may also be built as a loadable extension, not only as part of the main SQLite build. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Supported fact]` The SQL function `load_extension()` loads an SQLite extension, but extension loading is disabled by default and must first be enabled with `sqlite3_enable_load_extension()`. (https://sqlite.org/lang_corefunc.html)

`[Inference]` Because FTS5 can be either compiled in or provided as a loadable extension, compile-option checks tell you whether the current SQLite library was built with `SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5`, but they do not by themselves prove that FTS5 is currently registered on a specific connection. `PRAGMA module_list` is the stronger documented connection-level check. (https://sqlite.org/compile.html , https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html , https://sqlite.org/lang_corefunc.html , https://sqlite.org/pragma.html)

**External-Content FTS5 Tables**

`[Supported fact]` An external-content FTS5 table is created by setting `content=` to the name of a table, virtual table, or view in the same database; `content_rowid=` can override the default rowid column name used by FTS5. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Supported fact]` When FTS5 needs column values from an external-content table, it queries the content object by rowid, and it may also query it ordered ascending or descending by the content rowid. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Supported fact]` With external content, “all FTS5 functionality may be used,” but the user is responsible for keeping the full-text index consistent with the content object; if not, query results may be unpredictable. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Supported fact]` If a query against the external-content FTS5 table does not use the full-text index, such as one without `MATCH` or equivalent table-valued-function syntax, SQLite effectively passes that query through to the content table, so the FTS index does not affect the result. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Supported fact]` If a query does use the full-text index, FTS5 first gets matching rowids from the index and then looks up the corresponding column values in the content table. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Supported fact]` Triggers are one documented way to keep an external-content FTS5 table synchronized with its content table. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Supported fact]` Creating those triggers after the content table already contains rows does not backfill the FTS index; the triggers only keep later inserts, updates, and deletes synchronized. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Supported fact]` If the FTS index and content table become inconsistent, the documented `rebuild` command can discard the existing FTS index and rebuild it from the current content table. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Supported fact]` External-content FTS5 tables do not support `REPLACE` conflict handling; operations that specify `REPLACE` are handled using `ABORT`. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

**Uncertainty / Lack Of Good Evidence**

`[Lack of good evidence]` In the primary SQLite pages I reviewed, I did not find a dedicated single-purpose API documented as “detect whether FTS5 is available now on this connection” beyond the general mechanisms above: registered-module introspection (`PRAGMA module_list`), compile-option introspection, and extension loading.

# SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5

Here is the verbatim quote from the documentation:

**SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5**

> When this option is defined in the [amalgamation](amalgamation.html), version 5 of the full-text search engine ([fts5](fts5.html)) is added to the build automatically.

# FTS5 Runtime Support Detection and External Content Tables

## (1) Detecting/Enabling FTS5 Support at Runtime

### Compile-Time Options

FTS5 can be enabled in several ways:

**As part of SQLite:**
- Using configure: `--enable-fts5` flag when running the configure script
- By defining the preprocessor symbol `SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5` when compiling sqlite3.c
- "FTS5 is currently disabled by default for the source-tree configure script and enabled by default for the amalgamation configure script"

**As a loadable extension:**
The documentation states: "Alternatively, FTS5 may be built as a loadable extension."

### Runtime Detection

To check if FTS5 is available at runtime, use `sqlite3_compileoption_used()`:

```c
if (sqlite3_compileoption_used("ENABLE_FTS5")) {
    // FTS5 is available
}
```

Alternatively, query the compile options via SQL:

```sql
PRAGMA compile_options;
```

### Loading as Extension

If built as a loadable extension, load it with:

```c
sqlite3_load_extension(db, "fts5");
```

The extension has two entry points: `sqlite3_fts_init` or `sqlite3_fts5_init`.

---

## (2) External Content Tables: Complete Reference

### Overview and Creation

"An external content FTS5 table is created by setting the content option to the name of a table, virtual table or view (hereafter the 'content table') within the same database."

```sql
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE ft USING fts5(b, c, content='t1', content_rowid='a');
```

### How FTS5 Queries External Content

"Whenever column values are required by FTS5, it queries the content table as follows, with the rowid of the row for which values are required bound to the SQL variable:

```sql
SELECT <content_rowid>, <cols> FROM <content> WHERE <content_rowid> = ?;
```

In the above, <content> is replaced by the name of the content table. By default, <content_rowid> is replaced by the literal text "rowid". Or, if the "content_rowid" option is set within the CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE statement, by the value of that option."

# sqlite3_compileoption_used() Function

**What it does:**
"The sqlite3_compileoption_used() function returns 0 or 1 indicating whether the specified option was defined at compile time. The SQLITE_ prefix may be omitted from the option name passed to sqlite3_compileoption_used()."

**Availability:**
When `SQLITE_OMIT_COMPILEOPTION_DIAGS` is defined at compile time, the function is NOT available. Instead, it is replaced with a macro definition:

```c
# define sqlite3_compileoption_used(X) 0
```

This means the function call will simply return 0 when the diagnostic option is omitted.

# Section 2: Compiling and Using FTS5

## 2.1. Building FTS5 as part of SQLite

As of [version 3.9.0](releaselog/3_9_0.html) (2015-10-14), FTS5 is included as part of the SQLite [amalgamation](amalgamation.html). If using the canonical source tree, FTS5 is enabled by specifying the "--enable-fts5" option when running the configure script. (FTS5 is currently disabled by default for the source-tree configure script and enabled by default for the amalgamation configure script, but these defaults might change in the future.)

Or, if sqlite3.c is compiled using some other build system, by arranging for the SQLITE\_ENABLE\_FTS5 pre-processor symbol to be defined.

## 2.2. Building a Loadable Extension

Alternatively, FTS5 may be built as a loadable extension.

The canonical FTS5 source code consists of a series of \*.c and other files in the "ext/fts5" directory of the SQLite source tree. A build process reduces this to just two files - "fts5.c" and "fts5.h" - which may be used to build an SQLite loadable extension.

1.  Obtain the latest SQLite code from fossil.
2.  Create a Makefile as described in [How To Compile SQLite](howtocompile.html).
3.  Build the "fts5.c" target, which also creates fts5.h.

$ wget -c https://sqlite.org/src/tarball/SQLite-trunk.tgz?uuid=trunk -O SQLite-trunk.tgz
.... output ...
$ tar -xzf SQLite-trunk.tgz
$ cd SQLite-trunk
$ ./configure && make fts5.c
... lots of output ...
$ ls fts5.\[ch\]
fts5.c        fts5.h

The code in "fts5.c" may then be compiled into a loadable extension or statically linked into an application as described in [Compiling Loadable Extensions](loadext.html#build). There are two entry points defined, both of which do the same thing:

*   sqlite3\_fts\_init
*   sqlite3\_fts5\_init

The other file, "fts5.h", is not required to compile the FTS5 extension. It is used by applications that implement [custom FTS5 tokenizers or auxiliary functions](fts5.html#extending_fts5).

**PRAGMA compile_options;**

See also the [sqlite3_compileoption_get()](c3ref/compileoption_get.html) C/C++ interface and the [sqlite_compileoption_get()](lang_corefunc.html#sqlite_compileoption_get) SQL functions.

# sqlite_compileoption_used(X) and sqlite_compileoption_get(N)

## sqlite_compileoption_used(X)

> The sqlite_compileoption_used() SQL function is a wrapper around the [sqlite3_compileoption_used()](c3ref/compileoption_get.html) C/C++ function. When the argument X to sqlite_compileoption_used(X) is a string which is the name of a compile-time option, this routine returns true (1) or false (0) depending on whether or not that option was used during the build.

## sqlite_compileoption_get(N)

> The sqlite_compileoption_get() SQL function is a wrapper around the [sqlite3_compileoption_get()](c3ref/compileoption_get.html) C/C++ function. This routine returns the N-th compile-time option used to build SQLite or NULL if N is out of range. See also the [compile_options pragma](pragma.html#pragma_compile_options).

# Relevant FTS5 Documentation Excerpts

## (a) Responsibility for External Content Table Consistency

> It is the responsibility of the user to ensure that an FTS5 external content table (one with a non-empty content= option) is kept consistent with the content table itself (the table named by the content= option). If these are allowed to become inconsistent, then the results of queries against the FTS5 table may become unintuitive and appear inconsistent.

## (b) REPLACE Conflict Handling

> Like contentless tables, external content tables do not support REPLACE conflict handling. Any operations that specify REPLACE conflict handling are handled using ABORT.

## (c) The 'rebuild' Command

> This command first deletes the entire full-text index, then rebuilds it based on the contents of the table or [content table](fts5.html#external_content_tables). It is not available with [contentless tables](fts5.html#contentless_tables).

```
INSERT INTO ft(ft) VALUES('rebuild');
```

## (d) The 'delete' Command

> This command is only available with [external content](fts5.html#external_content_tables) and [contentless](fts5.html#contentless_tables) tables. It is used to delete the index entries associated with a single row from the full-text index. This command and the [delete-all](fts5.html#the_delete_all_command) command are the only ways to remove entries from the full-text index of a contentless table.
>
> In order to use this command to delete a row, the text value 'delete' must be inserted into the special column with the same name as the table. The rowid of the row to delete is inserted into the rowid column. The values inserted into the other columns must match the values currently stored in the table. For example:

```sql
_-- Insert a row with rowid=14 into the fts5 table._
INSERT INTO ft(rowid, a, b, c) VALUES(14, $a, $b, $c);

_-- Remove the same row from the fts5 table._
INSERT INTO ft(ft, rowid, a, b, c) VALUES('delete', 14, $a, $b, $c);
```

## Summary

Two separate questions: (1) how an application can tell at runtime whether FTS5 is usable, and (2) what SQLite actually promises — and pointedly does *not* promise — for `content=`-backed FTS5 tables.

---

## 1. Detecting FTS5 support at runtime

### What the primary docs actually say

The FTS5 documentation's "Compiling and Using FTS5" section describes only *build-time* enablement, not runtime detection. **Fact:** FTS5 ships in the amalgamation as of version 3.9.0 (2015-10-14); in the canonical source tree it is enabled with `--enable-fts5`, "Or, if sqlite3.c is compiled using some other build system, by arranging for the SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5 pre-processor symbol to be defined." The docs also note "FTS5 is currently disabled by default for the source-tree configure script and enabled by default for the amalgamation configure script, but these defaults might change in the future." ([fts5.html §2.1](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)) `compile.html` confirms: "When this option is defined in the amalgamation, version 5 of the full-text search engine (fts5) is added to the build automatically." ([compile.html](https://www.sqlite.org/compile.html))

**Fact:** FTS5 may alternatively be built as a loadable extension, with two equivalent entry points, `sqlite3_fts_init` and `sqlite3_fts5_init`. ([fts5.html §2.2](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html))

**Evidence gap to state plainly:** SQLite publishes no canonical "here is how to detect FTS5" recipe. Everything below is assembled from other primary pages, and I mark which parts are documented versus inferred.

### Method A — compile-option introspection (documented mechanism, partial coverage)

```sql
PRAGMA compile_options;                      -- look for the row 'ENABLE_FTS5'
SELECT sqlite_compileoption_used('ENABLE_FTS5');
```

- **Fact:** `PRAGMA compile_options` "returns the names of compile-time options used when building SQLite, one option per row. The 'SQLITE_' prefix is omitted from the returned option names." ([pragma.html](https://www.sqlite.org/pragma.html))
- **Fact:** `sqlite_compileoption_used(X)` "is a wrapper around the sqlite3_compileoption_used() C/C++ function… returns true (1) or false (0) depending on whether or not that option was used during the build." ([lang_corefunc.html](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_corefunc.html))
- **Fact (C API):** "The sqlite3_compileoption_used() function returns 0 or 1 indicating whether the specified option was defined at compile time. The SQLITE_ prefix may be omitted from the option name." ([c3ref/compileoption_get.html](https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/compileoption_get.html))
- **Documented limitation:** all of these disappear together. `SQLITE_OMIT_COMPILEOPTION_DIAGS` "is used to omit the compile-time option diagnostics available in SQLite, including the sqlite3_compileoption_used() and sqlite3_compileoption_get() C/C++ functions, the sqlite_compileoption_used() and sqlite_compileoption_get() SQL functions, and the compile_options pragma." ([compile.html](https://www.sqlite.org/compile.html)) In that build the C function is replaced by a macro that evaluates to `0`. ([c3ref/compileoption_get.html](https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/compileoption_get.html))
- **Inference (well-supported, not stated verbatim):** because this reports only what was *defined at compile time*, it will report absent for an FTS5 that was loaded at runtime as a loadable extension, and it will report `0` rather than "unknown" in an `SQLITE_OMIT_COMPILEOPTION_DIAGS` build. So a `0`/absent result is **not** proof that FTS5 is unavailable. I could not find primary documentation addressing this case directly.
- **Uncertainty:** the docs do not state that `--enable-fts5` results in the literal string `ENABLE_FTS5` appearing in `compile_options`. It is the obvious reading (the flag's job is to define `SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5`), but treat it as inference.

### Method B — module list (documented mechanism, connection-accurate)

```sql
SELECT 1 FROM pragma_module_list WHERE name = 'fts5';
```

- **Fact:** "This pragma returns a list of virtual table modules registered with the database connection." ([pragma.html](https://www.sqlite.org/pragma.html))
- **Fact:** it needs no special build flag today — `SQLITE_INTROSPECTION_PRAGMAS` "is obsolete. It used to enable some extra PRAGMA statements such as PRAGMA function_list, PRAGMA module_list, and PRAGMA pragma_list, but those pragmas are now all enabled by default." It can still be removed via `SQLITE_OMIT_INTROSPECTION_PRAGMAS`. ([compile.html](https://www.sqlite.org/compile.html))
- **Inference:** since it reflects modules *registered with the connection*, this is the method that correctly reports FTS5 loaded as an extension, which Method A cannot. The exact registered module name is not documented; `'fts5'` follows from the `USING fts5(...)` syntax used throughout the docs, and older SQLite (pre-3.16.0, when `pragma_*` table-valued functions arrived) will not support the `pragma_module_list` function form.

### Method C — functional probe (not documented; most reliable in practice)

Attempt `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE temp.fts5_probe USING fts5(x);` and treat an error as "unavailable." **This is my recommendation as the primary check**, with Method B as a cheaper pre-check. It is an inference from documented behavior, not a documented recipe — but it is the only approach that survives both the `SQLITE_OMIT_COMPILEOPTION_DIAGS` and the loadable-extension cases. Using `temp.` avoids writing to the main database.

## 2. External-content FTS5 tables: guarantees and limitations

### What it is

**Fact:** "An external content FTS5 table is created by setting the content option to the name of a table, virtual table or view (hereafter the 'content table') within the same database. Whenever column values are required by FTS5, it queries the content table as follows, with the rowid of the row for which values are required bound to the SQL variable: `SELECT <content_rowid>, <cols> FROM <content> WHERE <content_rowid> = ?;`" By default `<content_rowid>` is the literal text `rowid`, or the value of the `content_rowid` option if set. Full scans are served by `... ORDER BY <content_rowid> ASC|DESC`. ([fts5.html §4.4.3](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html#external_content_tables))

```sql
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE ft USING fts5(b, c, content='t1', content_rowid='a');
```

**Fact:** a view is explicitly supported as the content table — the docs show `content=v1` over a view combining a value with its locale. ([fts5.html §4.4.3](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html#external_content_tables))

### The central guarantee: there is none — consistency is yours to maintain

**Fact, verbatim:** "It is the responsibility of the user to ensure that an FTS5 external content table (one with a non-empty content= option) is kept consistent with the content table itself (the table named by the content= option). If these are allowed to become inconsistent, then the results of queries against the FTS5 table may become unintuitive and appear inconsistent." ([fts5.html §4.4.3](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html#external_content_tables))

**Fact:** the documented divergence behavior, from the docs' own worked examples — the index and the content table are consulted independently:

- Content table populated, index empty → `SELECT * FROM ft;` returns the rows (read passes through to the content table), while `SELECT rowid, t FROM ft('gold');` returns 0 rows.
- Index populated, content table empty → `SELECT * FROM ft;` returns 0 rows, while the MATCH query returns a row whose column value is `NULL`. ([fts5.html §4.4.3](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html#external_content_tables))

So the failure mode is silent wrong answers, not an error.

### Ordering requirement for deletes and updates

**Fact, verbatim:** on a DELETE, "the current values are retrieved by querying the content table… The values retrieved are then passed to the table's configured tokenizer, which extracts from them the list of tokens that need to be removed from the FTS index. If the retrieved values do not match the set of entries in the FTS index for the row, then some tokens may be left in the FTS index, leading to inconsistent query results later on. In practice, this means that to delete a row from both the content table and the FTS5 external content table, the FTS5 table must be updated first (so that the content table row is still available to it). In FTS5, an UPDATE statement is implemented as a DELETE followed by an INSERT of the new values. It follows that when UPDATEing a row in both the content table and FTS5 external content table, the FTS5 table must be updated first." ([fts5.html §4.4.3](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html#external_content_tables))

**Practical consequence (inference):** an `AFTER DELETE` / `AFTER UPDATE` trigger works because the trigger body sees `old.*` values; the requirement is really that FTS5 be handed the *old* values, not that the physical row still exist.

### Documented limitations

| Limitation | Status |
|---|---|
| No REPLACE conflict handling: "Like contentless tables, external content tables do not support REPLACE conflict handling. Any operations that specify REPLACE conflict handling are handled using ABORT." | Fact ([fts5.html](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html#external_content_tables)) |
| Creating sync triggers does not backfill: "triggers are only fired when rows are inserted, updated or deleted in the content table… as creating the triggers does not copy existing rows from the content table into the FTS index." | Fact ([fts5.html](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html#external_content_tables)) |
| `'delete'` command values must match: "If the values 'inserted' into the text columns as part of a 'delete' command are not the same as those currently stored within the table, the results may be unpredictable… some full-text index entries may not be correctly deleted, or FTS5 may try to remove index entries that do not exist." | Fact ([fts5.html §6](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html#the_delete_command)) |
| `integrity-check` does **not** check against the content table by default: "For an external content table, the contents of the index are only compared to the contents of the external content table if the value specified for the rank column is 1." Discrepancies fail with `SQLITE_CORRUPT_VTAB`. | Fact ([fts5.html §6.7](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)) |

Use `INSERT INTO ft(ft, rank) VALUES('integrity-check', 1);` — the plain form only verifies internal index structure.

### Repair and the sanctioned sync pattern

**Fact:** `'rebuild'` "first deletes the entire full-text index, then rebuilds it based on the contents of the table or content table. It is not available with contentless tables." ([fts5.html §6](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html#the_rebuild_command)) The docs name it as the remedy: "In this, and any other situation where the FTS index and its content table have become inconsistent, the 'rebuild' command may be used." ([fts5.html §4.4.3](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html#external_content_tables))

**Fact:** `'delete'` and `'delete-all'` are "only available with external content and contentless tables"; `delete-all` "deletes all entries from the full-text index." ([fts5.html §6](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html#the_delete_all_command))

The documented trigger recipe ([fts5.html §4.4.3](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html#external_content_tables)):

```sql
CREATE TRIGGER t1_ai AFTER INSERT ON t1 BEGIN
  INSERT INTO fts_idx(rowid, b, c) VALUES (new.a, new.b, new.c);
END;
CREATE TRIGGER t1_ad AFTER DELETE ON t1 BEGIN
  INSERT INTO fts_idx(fts_idx, rowid, b, c) VALUES('delete', old.a, old.b, old.c);
END;
CREATE TRIGGER t1_au AFTER UPDATE ON t1 BEGIN
  INSERT INTO fts_idx(fts_idx, rowid, b, c) VALUES('delete', old.a, old.b, old.c);
  INSERT INTO fts_idx(rowid, b, c) VALUES (new.a, new.b, new.c);
END;
```

Run `INSERT INTO fts_idx(fts_idx) VALUES('rebuild');` once after creating the triggers over an already-populated table.

### Contrast with contentless tables (`content=''`)

Distinct feature, often confused with external content. **Fact:** contentless tables "do not support UPDATE or DELETE statements, or INSERT statements that do not supply a non-NULL value for the rowid field," and "Attempting to read any column value except the rowid from a contentless FTS5 table returns an SQL NULL value." As of version 3.43.0, contentless-delete tables (`content='', contentless_delete=1`) support DELETE and `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO`, and support UPDATE "but only if new values are supplied for all user-defined columns"; they do **not** support the `'delete'` command. ([fts5.html §4.4.1–4.4.2](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html#contentless_tables))

- **Not documented:** whether `highlight()`/`snippet()` degrade gracefully on external-content tables whose content row is missing. The `NULL`-column behavior above makes `NULL`/empty output the likely result, but I found no primary statement, so I won't assert it.
- **Not documented:** whether SQLite validates the existence or shape of the content table at `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE` time. The docs describe only query-time access, and I found no statement either way.
